title: Narrow-Leaved Ash: Ancient Narrow-Leaved Ashes You Can Visit
meta_description: A riverside ash of dry southern Europe, once pollarded for fodder. Girona has one 5.90 metres round; Barcelona grew the tallest ever measured in Catalonia.
intro: Fraxinus angustifolia is the ash of southern Europe, a riverside species that follows watercourses through country too dry for its northern cousin, and for centuries it was pollarded for fodder and tool handles rather than left to grow free. That habit shapes the three mapped here differently. Girona's, at L'Aulet in Vidreres, carries a 5.90 metre trunk built from decades of repeated cutting, a short massive base under a crown that is all regrowth. Barcelona's grew the opposite way, straight up a Montjuic quarry pit whose damp, sheltered air let it reach 29 metres, the tallest of its species recorded anywhere in Catalonia. Leiden's stands furthest from home, planted in a Dutch botanical garden around 1818 and grafted, the swelling from that graft still visible after two centuries. Ash dieback is moving through Europe regardless of species, which makes a healthy veteran worth finding while it stands.
